transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Well… I’m not sure if it’s a big enough thing to bring in, but it’s been bothering me more than I’d like. Since I started helping with the safety trainings at work, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing things out—like how wrinkly and uneven they look. And then I’ll see myself in the newsletter photos and start thinking my face looks crooked.

People tell me they don’t really see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but I can’t seem to stop noticing it.
Do you find yourself concerned about other parts of your body as well, or does it mostly center on your hands and face?

Mostly my hands and my face, I think. The hands started standing out to me more with the safety trainings, because I’m pointing at things and I notice how wrinkly or uneven they look. And then with my face, it’s more when I see those newsletter photos—I start thinking it looks crooked. Other people say they don’t really see it, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but those are the main things.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking photos, or adjusting your hands or face when you're worried about how they look?

I mean… a little, yes. Not anything too extreme, I don’t think. Before I have to teach a class or go to one of the senior-center workshops, I’ll usually stop in the bathroom and check the mirror a few times. I put lotion on my hands, kind of turn my face different ways to see if it looks okay.

Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker, “Do I look all right?” which I know probably sounds silly. It can make me run a little behind, but I still get where I’m supposed to go.
Do these concerns about how your hands and face look ever cause you a lot of stress or make it harder for you to do things you need to do?

It hasn’t stopped me from doing things, really. I still go to work, and I still do the volunteer workshops. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything.

But… it does slow me down sometimes, especially before trainings. I’ll take longer getting ready or checking how I look than I probably need to. And I’ve noticed I’ve started trying to stay out of photos when I can, or I’ll hesitate before going to social things I used to just enjoy without thinking so much. I guess it does stress me more than I’d like to admit.

latest_inference.note: The patient's concerns are primarily focused on specific body parts (face and hands) and involve preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in appearance, causing significant distress and some functional impairment. This aligns more strongly with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). Additionally, anxiety around appearance and repetitive behaviors could also support a diagnosis of phobic anxiety disorder (F40.00). Other conditions like obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.2), major depressive disorder (F32.0), and dissociative disorders (F44.5) are less consistent with the presentation and have been ruled out.
